title: Homotopy normal form over the local ring at a good residue point
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $P$ a cochain complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [def-pc-derived-category] with finite free terms [def-weil-pbc-free-module], supported in degrees $0$ through $d\in\mathbb N$. Fix $y\in Y$ and $i,r\in\mathbb N$. Suppose the termwise pullback [def-pc-derived-pullback] to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ has zero cohomology in every nonnegative degree different from $i$, and finite locally free cohomology of rank $r$ in degree $i$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and let $s:S\to Y$ be the canonical morphism. Then $s^*P$ is homotopy equivalent to $s^*(\mathcal O_Y^r[-i])$, where $\mathcal O_Y^r[-i]$ denotes the single cochain complex in degree $i$. A homotopy equivalence means two chain maps whose composites are chain homotopic to the respective identities.

proof.text: Choose bases of all terms. Pull back to S = Spec(O_{Y,y}) and use the affine quasicoherent module-sheaf correspondence on these free terms to obtain a bounded finite free complex of O_{Y,y}-modules. The factorization fromSpecResidueField(y) = Spec(residue quotient) followed by fromSpecStalk(y) identifies its termwise reduction with the residue complex in the hypothesis.

Reverse the integer grading and split off a two-term identity summand at every unit differential entry using lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-unit-entry-splits. The homotopy on that summand is the inverse identity from its target to its source. Include the complement and project onto it to obtain a homotopy equivalence. The sum of the finite ranks in degrees 0 through d decreases by two; induction terminates with a bounded free complex whose differential entries all lie in the maximal ideal.

Residue reduction of the remainder has zero differential. The removed identity complexes are contractible after reduction, so its cohomology equals the assumed residue cohomology. In negative degrees support makes the terms zero; in nonnegative degrees the residue dimensions are zero off i and r at i. A finite free module reduces to a vector space of its free rank. Thus all remaining terms are zero except a free rank-r term in degree i; when i > d this forces r = 0. Identify that term with the standard free module and compose the homotopy equivalences. Associated sheaves and the pullback-free and pullback-single isomorphisms give exactly the two complexes of the statement.
